issues.description: `inv_stray_in_node` incorrectly requires every stray entry to retain a live node, excluding the true-stray state created when a node is removed and waits for recycling.
issues.rationale: The model uses a false stray for a node still present in the page table and a true stray for a removed node awaiting reclamation. `protocol_deallocate` removes `nid` from `nodes`, replaces its false stray with a true stray, and therefore immediately produces a state that violates `inv_stray_in_node`'s implication from every stray key to `nodes.contains_key(nid)`. The human reviewer identified this incorrect invariant, the author agreed, and the final head removes it in favor of tracking genuinely free physical addresses separately.
issues.verification: source-only; historical Verus was not executed. Independently checked the selected review commit and confirmed that a valid deallocation transition contradicts this invariant; its inductive proof remains admitted. The invariant is removed and the address-resource model is changed in the final head.

issues.description: `wf_cursors` validates only cursor keys that happen to exist and does not require every valid CPU to own a cursor token.
issues.rationale: The invariant's `dom().all(...)` implication is one-way: existing cursor keys must be valid and well formed, but a valid CPU may be absent from the map. Every per-CPU protocol transition removes that CPU's cursor token, so a model state satisfying `wf_cursors` can nevertheless leave a valid CPU unable to take any cursor transition. The human CHANGES_REQUESTED review called out the missing reverse coverage, and the final head fixes it by adding `forall valid_cpu(...) ==> cursors.contains_key(cpu)` together with finite-domain tracking.
